set.per_unit_cap: Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g)(1)(C): where a property qualifies only because 90% or more of occupants are lower income households (no bond, government loan or grant financing under (A) and no tax credits under (B)), the total exemption is capped at $20,000,000 of assessed value. Projects financed under (A) or receiving LIHTC under (B) are outside the cap.
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: the Assessor landing page (source_url) carries no welfare exemption detail; statute text read on california.public.law. 214 contains no construction-period language (see 214.1 for property in the course of construction), so the next_deadline note citing 214(g) for that should be checked.

reason: Material: per_unit_cap tied the $20,000,000 cap to limited partnerships qualifying through the managing general partner test, but 214(g)(1)(C) applies it to properties qualifying solely through the 90% lower-income occupancy test.
